name: Sol
intro: A warm, compact forecast built around a satin sun and a frosted horizon. Keep the weather legible while the atmosphere stays quiet.
direction: Ivory shell, orange satin disc, frosted lower plane, citron selected controls and charcoal type. The disc stays behind the data; labels never become part of a shader.
font: Inter for data and controls. Preserve the source’s generous temperature scale.
baseline: Lisbon · Thu, Jun 18 · 28°C · Sunset 20:58 · Today selected.
observations: The source has seven interactive targets: More, two unit choices and four day tabs. City, date, temperature, condition and sunset are read-only content.
The warm sun is decorative. Its position must not imply a measured sun altitude without a defined data mapping.
New dates and temperatures in state specifications are fixed review fixtures, not a live forecast.

motion: On a committed day change, crossfade the condition illustration in 180 ms. A future satin sun shader may shift its highlight by at most 2% over a slow 12-second cycle while visible. It is decorative, paused offscreen, and completely static for reduced motion. No temperature count-up.
assets: Extract or recreate the orange sun disc, a separate frosted plane and a static fallback. Deliver transparent artwork without any text, tabs, icon labels or shadows that cross the component edge. Keep one stable camera and lighting direction. A bitmap cannot yield a true 3D mesh; reconstruct if a 3D material is required.
react: WeatherCard receives location, forecastByDate, selectedDate, unit, status and onDateChange/onUnitChange/onLocationChange. Canonical temperatures stay in Celsius; formatted labels are derived. Cache is keyed by location and date, not by rendered unit.
invariants: Exactly one day and one unit are selected.
A stale forecast is labelled with its actual update time.
alternative: Compact horizontal forecast: move the sun to a narrow leading area, keep four dates visible and preserve all unit/location controls. This is a layout proposal, not an additional exported screen.
archive_note: The five saved variations cover everyday forecast, weekend planning, golden-hour planning, garden rain and cooler-hour planning. Their controls need context-specific data; a golden-hour window is not a generic temperature tab.
title: Sol — Weather card

common.responsive: Let text reflow at 200% zoom. Keep every control operable by touch and keyboard, with a minimum 44 × 44 CSS-pixel hit area as a WDA design target. Preserve the component’s natural aspect ratio in raster review; the implementation reflows content rather than scaling text to fit.
common.focus: Use a visible 2px high-contrast focus ring with 3px offset. Never make hover the only way to discover or activate a control.
common.reduced_motion: Remove translation, rotation, parallax and looping animation. Selection, loading labels and focus remain visible; use an instant swap or an opacity change of at most 100 ms.
common.scroll: Keep the component in normal document flow. Do not hijack scrolling or drive selected values from scroll position. Pause optional decorative motion while offscreen.
common.persistence: The review explorer describes behavior; it does not send requests or store user data. Production persistence belongs to the host application and must reconcile pending/error states.

branches: Sat 20 and Sun 21 follow the same day-selection contract as Friday; their fixture values are 27°C/81°F at 21:00 and 26°C/79°F at 21:01. In Fahrenheit, selecting Friday shows 84°F. Do not reset unit on a date change.

Change location opens a labelled search field. Empty input shows no results; pending search exposes loading; zero results offers edit; Arrow keys select and Enter commits a result. Escape/cancel keeps Lisbon. New-location failure retains labelled old data and Retry. This supporting host search is documented rather than a sixth image.

First-load failure has no cached forecast: show an error and Retry, never 0°. Refreshing labels the current data as updating and prevents duplicate requests. Close uses the × control, Escape or outside click.
state_note: Five designed state images. Review actions are labelled simulations; host integrations and extra data combinations are specified below.
descriptive: Title, helper copy, count, price, divider and artwork are descriptive unless the control inventory assigns an action. Decorative layers use pointer-events:none and aria-hidden. Read-only regions have no hover lift, pointer cursor or tab stop.

name: Gather
intro: A small selection tool with a rich material personality. Its warmth comes from four tactile avatars and a dark cocoa surface, with clear selection feedback.
direction: Cocoa panel, cream checkmarks and rose, amber, moss and burgundy objects. Keep the floating trigger connected to the list and preserve generous row spacing.
font: Inter for names, roles and count. Names lead; roles remain secondary but readable.
baseline: Lena Ortiz, Noah Bell and Amara Chen selected; Eli Brooks unselected. Trigger and footer both show 3.
observations: The original trigger plus four person rows are interactive. Avatars, headings, roles and count are descriptive; tapping an avatar activates its row, not a separate profile.
Selection takes effect immediately in this compact picker. Closing is dismissal, not undo; the UI must never suggest an unimplemented Apply step.
Storycircle’s older trigger shows three spheres although two readers are selected. Plotcrew shows three for four helpers without a +1 label. These are recorded archive issues.

motion: Open with a 140 ms opacity change and a 4px vertical offset. Checkmarks settle in 100 ms; avatars move only when the selected set changes. Do not continuously spin or float people. Preserve list height while an error appears beneath the footer.
assets: Prepare four separate material spheres: rose ceramic, amber glass, moss stone and burgundy ribbed wood. Reuse the identical sphere for a person in the row and trigger. Export transparent assets with matched camera, light and baseline. No portrait replacements or names baked into pixels.
react: TeamPicker receives people, selectedIds, open, saveStatus and onSelectionChange. Use a controlled Popover plus native checkboxes. Count is selectedIds.length; displayed avatars are selectedIds for the four-person study; use a labelled overflow count only when the layout actually requires it. Store attempted and last-confirmed sets for save errors.
invariants: 0 selected gives zero avatars and a zero count.
All four selected shows four or a truthful three-plus-one summary.
Closing preserves current selection; failed save never claims success.
alternative: For a long directory, add a labelled search field and a scrollable list with a fixed summary. Selection remains by stable person ID across filters. This is a future layout option; the original four-person picker remains primary.
archive_note: Dinner guests, garden helpers, book-club readers and a recording crew apply the same selection behavior. Invitation copy in Tablemate does not prove invitations were sent; production must distinguish selected from invited.

motion: Only the hovered material lifts 2px; on selection the ring crossfades in 120 ms. Shuffle crossfades the set over 180 ms with no mixing of old labels and new artwork. There is no ambient rotation. Under reduced motion, update the entire set immediately.
assets: Prepare five independent transparent material spheres plus a common shadow. Name files by stable material ID. Keep shape, camera, size and light fixed across every set. Do not extract labels or selected rings into the assets: those are DOM/CSS layers.
react: MaterialPalette receives materials, selectedMaterialId and onSelect/onShuffle/onUndo. Store a full previous snapshot for undo; never derive identity from current array position. Use a fieldset of labelled radios, keeping shuffle outside the group.
invariants: Exactly five named materials and one selected ring.
Shuffle updates names, assets and IDs together.
Undo restores both palette and selection.
alternative: On narrow surfaces, reflow to three swatches then two with the shuffle action below. Do not make the swatches too small to tap or force a long horizontal drag for core choices.

name: Roam
intro: An editorial membership card with a clear decision at its centre. Keep the ribbon and sculptural feature objects expressive while the plan and price remain authoritative.
direction: Tall ivory panel, serif headline, coral ribbon, warm feature cells and a burgundy CTA. Give plan changes space; the whole panel should not jump in height.
font: DM Serif Display for editorial headings; Inter for prices, tabs, features and buttons. These are proposed implementation mappings, not verified raster font identities.
baseline: Everyday selected; $24 / month; CTA Choose Everyday; four feature tiles.
observations: Weekender, Everyday, Worldwide and the primary CTA are controls. Feature tiles are informational in the original; detail disclosure is a proposed extension.

Weekender $12 and Worldwide $48 with their new benefit copy are proposed design fixtures. Everyday $24 is inherited from the original. None is a verified purchasable product. Production must inject a verified catalogue, currency, availability and tax treatment.
